your clothes were poor but neat,  
always caring for the spirit in prayer.  

7.  
When both your parents were dead,  
you received from their inheritance a very great treasure,  
which you did not waste uselessly  
or lock away in an iron chest.  

8.  
To the poor you gave generously,  
because you did not keep it as your own,  
but as steward appointed by the Lord,  
whereby this deed of yours is also told:  

9.  
In Patara there was a poor nobleman,  
who had three beautiful daughters by his wife;  
but when they had grown old,  
he could no longer provide for their maintenance.  

10.  
So he gave them advice,  
which was deadly harm to their souls,  
that for a piece of money they would stain their purity  
with dishonor.  

11.  
As soon as Saint Nicholas heard this,  
he went by night to the very house,  
threw the window open, a bag with gold,  
with which one daughter was supported.  

12.  
Again he returned home once more,  
and threw gold through the window again;  
so the second daughter got married,  
so great was the power of this hidden gold.  

13.  
He also thought of the third daughter,  
and one night brought money into the house,  
with which he saved her body in distress  
and her soul from death.  

14.  
O wise and merciful prelate,  
you know our slippery state,  
by which our careless youth  
is soon carried away from their innocent virtue.  

15.  
Grant us from God a devout disposition,  
that always purely does His will;  
give us the gold of love in our shoe,  
so we escape the punishment of God’s rod.  
Because, if on the night before giving,  
it finds some sugar in it,  
some money, some joy, some more or less,  
according to what it has lived by  
the will of father and mother:  
for if it has too much shaved the beast  
and has been too bad,  
Saint Nicholas will put, in his shoe,  
instead of money, a piece of coal.']
